logline: Five blocks took Kolmogorov flow from worse than predicting nothing (1.063) to 0.0412: first an honest residual, then the capacity to use it, then knowing when the loss had stopped ranking fields.

b00.headline: b00 — control: the KF baseline, measured as it is (1.063)
b00.thrust: No design work: the task's plain-MLP PINN, trained once for its full wall clock at seed 0. It is the yardstick every later block is measured against.
findings: The baseline scores above 1.0: predicting u = v = 0 everywhere would do better, so the network is worse than predicting nothing.

b01.headline: b01 — separable PINN, causal weighting and SOAP: 1.063 → 0.840
b01.thrust: Forked from the baseline rather than tuned on it: b00 showed a structural failure, a field pinned to its initial condition, so tuning the plain MLP was pointless. Five changes went in together: a separable velocity-vorticity network, a periodic embedding, a hard initial condition, causal weighting and the SOAP optimiser.
findings: A pseudo-spectral surrogate of the same flow, built as a diagnostic, was the block's most useful product: it shows where the error lives.
The error is a propagation failure: the field is right near t = 0 and drifts away later.
The residual does not single out the true solution: the trained network's residual is far lower than the true field's.

b02.headline: b02 — a weak (Fourier-Galerkin) residual in the velocity norm: 0.840 → 0.131
b02.thrust: Forked from b01's champion idea, not its code. b01 had measured that the trained network's residual beats the true solution's, and then kept tuning; b02 read that as the residual being wrong and replaced the pointwise vorticity residual with its Fourier-Galerkin form, measured in the velocity norm.
findings: The residual was the bug, and it is fixable: the weak form in the velocity norm cut the error by a factor of six.
The test space must be complete: too few Fourier modes leave most of the grid's degrees of freedom unconstrained.
With an honest residual, causal weighting stops being a workaround and pays off again.

b03.headline: b03 — CP rank and the ε·NT gate: 0.131 → 0.0416
b03.thrust: Forked from b02's champion. b02 fixed the residual's formulation but left the network small, on the view that capacity was not the problem. b03 tested that directly with a rank sweep, and separated the causal gate's strength from its nominal ε.
findings: CP rank was the binding constraint: b02's advice not to buy capacity was wrong.
The causal gate's strength is ε·NT, not ε: change the time slices and the gate changes with them.
Faster steps bought nothing: two clean throughput wins left the score where it was.

candidates.b03_scan: training chunk in one jitted loop

b04.headline: b04 — the weak residual has stopped ranking fields: 0.0416 → 0.0412
b04.thrust: Forked from b03's champion. The score moved by less than seed noise; the block's product is a diagnosis. It measured whether a lower weak residual still meant a better field, and ruled out the cheaper explanations one by one.
findings: The gain is within seed noise: a second seed of the same two candidates spans 0.0424–0.0428.
The decisive measurement: at this level the weak residual no longer ranks fields by their error.
Aliasing, quadrature and capacity were each excluded with one cheap experiment.
